chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: In JavaScript, Array Mutator methods modify the original array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The Push method adds one or more elements to the end of an array, then returns the new

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: length of the array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The Pop method removes the last element from an array and returns that element.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The Shift method removes the first element from an array and returns the element.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The Unshift method adds one or more elements to the beginning of an array, then returns

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: the new length of the array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The Splice method adds and or removes elements from an array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The first parameter defines the position where the element should be added or removed.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The second parameter defines how many elements should be removed.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: All other parameters are the new elements to be added.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: It returns an array with the deleted items.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Here's an example where we are adding or essentially replacing two elements at the index of 1 and

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: the item count of 2.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Here the Splice method returns a new array containing the deleted items and adds the

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: new items in their place.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: And here's an example where we are simply removing an element at the index of 3.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The Sort method sorts the elements of an array in place and returns the array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Note that this method sorts by character order.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: So it sorts words, but if we try to sort the numbers 20 and 100, it would put 100 before

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: 20 since 1 is less than 2.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: We could, however, use Sort with a compare function to get the desired result.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The Reverse method simply reverses the order of the elements in an array and returns the

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Sort and Reverse can be combined to provide a descending sort of the array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The CopyWithin method copies a sequence of array elements to another location in the

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: same array and returns it without modifying its length.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The first parameter is the target index.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The second parameter, which is optional, is the index at which to start copying elements

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: from.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: And the third parameter, which is also optional, is the index at which to end copying elements

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: from up to but not including.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Negative numbers start counting from the end of the array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: In this example, our target is index 1, and the start is implied to be 0, and the end

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: is implied to be the entire length of the array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: So we are copying all of the items into the array starting at index 1 and replacing whatever

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: was there.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Here we are still targeting index 1, but we have specified the start to be index 3, which

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: happens to be the end of the array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: So here we will only copy index 3 into index 1, replacing it.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Now we are targeting index 0 and starting from index 1 to index 3.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Index 3 is the end of the array but will not be included in the copy.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: The Fill method changes all elements in an array to a static value, from a start index

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: to an end index.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Then it returns the modified array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Negative numbers start counting from the end of the array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: So without including the start and end parameters, the entire array will be filled with the same

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: value.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Including the start parameter will start filling from the start index throughout the rest of

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: the array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: Including the end parameter will start filling from the start index and stop before the end

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Mutator Methods
chunks.text: index.

text: In JavaScript, Array Mutator methods modify the original array. The Push method adds one or more elements to the end of an array, then returns the new length of the array. The Pop method removes the last element from an array and returns that element. The Shift method removes the first element from an array and returns the element. The Unshift method adds one or more elements to the beginning of an array, then returns the new length of the array. The Splice method adds and or removes elements from an array. The first parameter defines the position where the element should be added or removed. The second parameter defines how many elements should be removed. All other parameters are the new elements to be added. It returns an array with the deleted items. Here's an example where we are adding or essentially replacing two elements at the index of 1 and the item count of 2. Here the Splice method returns a new array containing the deleted items and adds the new items in their place. And here's an example where we are simply removing an element at the index of 3. The Sort method sorts the elements of an array in place and returns the array. Note that this method sorts by character order. So it sorts words, but if we try to sort the numbers 20 and 100, it would put 100 before 20 since 1 is less than 2. We could, however, use Sort with a compare function to get the desired result. The Reverse method simply reverses the order of the elements in an array and returns the array. Sort and Reverse can be combined to provide a descending sort of the array. The CopyWithin method copies a sequence of array elements to another location in the same array and returns it without modifying its length. The first parameter is the target index. The second parameter, which is optional, is the index at which to start copying elements from. And the third parameter, which is also optional, is the index at which to end copying elements from up to but not including. Negative numbers start counting from the end of the array. In this example, our target is index 1, and the start is implied to be 0, and the end is implied to be the entire length of the array. So we are copying all of the items into the array starting at index 1 and replacing whatever was there. Here we are still targeting index 1, but we have specified the start to be index 3, which happens to be the end of the array. So here we will only copy index 3 into index 1, replacing it. Now we are targeting index 0 and starting from index 1 to index 3. Index 3 is the end of the array but will not be included in the copy. The Fill method changes all elements in an array to a static value, from a start index to an end index. Then it returns the modified array. Negative numbers start counting from the end of the array. So without including the start and end parameters, the entire array will be filled with the same value. Including the start parameter will start filling from the start index throughout the rest of the array. Including the end parameter will start filling from the start index and stop before the end index. This has been a 90-ish second JavaScript January.
